summary: git init turns a folder into a repository. git status tells you what changed and what Git will do next.
notes: git init makes a hidden .git folder that stores the whole history.
Untracked files exist in the folder but Git is not saving their history yet.
Run git status often. It also suggests the next command to run.
pitfall: Running git init in your home folder instead of the project folder makes Git track everything you own. Run it inside the project folder.
setup_note: Starts in an empty folder named project.
